# Weighted base-centerpoint filtering does not repair the entropy escort selector

The proposed rule retains only integer bases p whose weighted atomic
halfspace depth for the fiber volumes is at least M/2^n, then selects
the continuous base-mean entropy escort center y_p. This rule is FALSE.
The examples below have one integer coordinate and a UNIQUE qualifying
base. Its escort point fails OC in both continuous dimensions1 and2.
The original bodies have explicit separate safe centers.

The actual geometric family is archived in
`candidate 25b281541ed968f0`.
What is new here is the exact different escort center and the fact that
EVERY weighted-centerpoint-qualified escort fails. The earlier archived
source tested a different centroid rule. Neither is an OC counterexample.

## 1. One actual nonaffine family and its unique qualifying base

Fix d>=1, 0<a<1, let Q=[0,1]^(d-1), and put

    k=(3-a)/4,
    A=[k-a/2,k+a/2] times Q at base -1,
    K=[0,1] times Q          at base  0,
    B=[k-1/2,k+1/2] times Q at base  1.                 (1)

For d=1 omit Q. Their volumes are a,1,1 and

    (A+B)/2=[(1-a)/2,1] times Q subset K.               (2)

Consequently their lifted convex hull C is a compact full-dimensional
convex body in R^(1+d), with EXACTLY these three integer fibers and
original mixed mass

    M=2+a.                                             (3)

Endpoint fibers are extreme base sections; every endpoint interpolation
at base0 already lies in K by(2). There are no other integer bases.
All three fiber volumes are strictly below M/2. Their continuous
centroids are(k,1/2,...,1/2),(1/2,...,1/2),(k,1/2,...,1/2).
As k>1/2, this actual centroid graph is nonaffine.

At base -1 a pure-base halfspace isolates mass a<M/2, and at base1
one isolates mass1<M/2. At base0 every containing base halfspace has
mass at least min(a+1,2)=a+1>M/2. Thus the unique weighted integer
centerpoint at the required level M/2^1 is p=0. Maximizing entropy
among the qualified bases or choosing ANY qualified base gives the
same candidate: there is no tie or untested alternative.

## 2. Exact escort point and one actual defeating cap

For the base-mean entropy with exponent(d+1)/(d+2), put

    w=((a^(1/(d+2))+1)/2)^(d+2),
    E_0=1+2w,
    y_d(a)=[1/2+2w k]/(1+2w).                          (4)

These are the exact formulas proved in
`candidate f3dc7a372eeb1eae`,
Section2. The escort endpoint masses are w/(1+2w) each; its middle
mass is1/(1+2w). The selected point is

    Y=(0,y_d(a),1/2,...,1/2).

Since y_d(a) is a strict convex combination of1/2 and k, it lies
strictly between them and is an actual interior middle-fiber point.
The closed ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x): x_1-z>=y_d(a) }                         (5)

passes through Y. At base -1 its threshold is y_d(a)-1<0, strictly
below min A=(3-3a)/4>0, so it captures ALL of A. At base1 its threshold
is y_d(a)+1>3/2, strictly above max B=(5-a)/4<5/4, so it captures
NONE of B. It properly cuts K, with null boundary. Its exact mass is

    mu(H)=a+1-y_d(a).                                  (6)

No supporting-face convention or claim of global criticality is used.
One such actual cap suffices to refute the candidate.

## 3. Exact interval certificate

Take d=1 and a=1/8. Then

    A=[21/32,25/32],  K=[0,1],  B=[7/32,39/32],
    (A+B)/2=[7/16,1],
    k=23/32,  w=27/64,  E_0=59/32,
    y_1(a)=1133/1888,  M=17/8.

The unique qualified escort therefore has an actual cap of mass

    mu(H)=991/1888 < 1003/1888=M/4.

Its normalized depth is at most

    991/4012 = 1/4 - 3/1003 < Gamma_1/2.                (7)

All data and every inequality are rational.

## 4. Exact positive planar certificate

Take d=2 and a=1/81. Then the full-dimensional planar fibers are

    A=[20/27,61/81] times[0,1],
    K=[0,1]^2,
    B=[20/81,101/81] times[0,1],
    (A+B)/2=[40/81,1] times[0,1].

Here a^(1/4)=1/3, so

    k=121/162,  w=16/81,  E_0=113/81,
    pi_-=pi_+=16/113,  pi_0=81/113,
    y_2(a)=10433/18306,  M=163/81.

The actual cap(5) has mass8099/18306 and normalized mass

    mu(H)/M=8099/36838
           =2/9-785/331542 < Gamma_2/2.                (8)

This is an actual compact three-dimensional ambient convex body with
all three positive planar integer fibers retained. Pure-base depth
filtering cannot discard p=0 or admit an endpoint at the required
M/2 threshold.

## 5. Separate safe centers and exact scope

At Y_*=(0,1/2,...,1/2), retain the whole middle K, the endpoint A and
its reflection through Y_* in the endpoint base1. The reflected
first-coordinate interval is

    [(1-a)/4,(1+3a)/4] subset B_1.

The other coordinates Q are invariant under their reflections. This
retained mixed measure is centrally symmetric about Y_*, with total
mass1+2a. Every containing closed ambient halfspace therefore captures
at least(1+2a)/2 of this retained measure, including pure-base normals.
Thus the ORIGINAL normalized depth at Y_* is at least

    (1+2a)/(2(2+a))>1/4>=Gamma_d/2.                    (9)

For the two certificates this is respectively5/17 and83/326. These
are explicit all-halfspace lower bounds at actual points, so the
failures(7),(8) concern only the proposed qualified escort selector.

The arithmetic filter fixes the earlier heavy-endpoint error in the
T,3T,4T example, but it does not fix the continuous escort's displacement
inside the uniquely admissible middle fiber. The current source closes
this selector route; it does not suggest a universal repair based only
on the absence of these two examples.
